scenarios.title: A spell cast for its cleave cost loses its bracketed text
decisions: A casts Path of Peril for its cleave cost {4}{W}{B}, tapping all six lands.
Both players pass; the spell resolves.

variants.label: cleave
variants.expected: The bracketed text is removed, so the spell destroys all creatures: Savannah Lions, Hill Giant and Grizzly Bears all move to their owners' graveyards.

variants.label: mana_cost
variants.delta: A casts Path of Peril for its mana cost {1}{B}{B}, tapping three Swamps.
variants.expected: The spell destroys only creatures with mana value 2 or less: Savannah Lions and Grizzly Bears are destroyed, Hill Giant (mana value 4) stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.title: Cleaving removes a targeting restriction, so a spell has a legal target it would not otherwise have
decisions: A casts Fierce Retribution for its cleave cost {5}{W} targeting Grizzly Bears (which is not attacking), tapping all six Plains.
Both players pass; the spell resolves.

variants.label: cleave
variants.expected: The cast is legal because the text 'attacking' is removed: Fierce Retribution destroys Grizzly Bears, which moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: mana_cost
variants.delta: A tries to cast Fierce Retribution for its mana cost {1}{W}.
variants.expected: The cast is not legal: the spell needs a target attacking creature and none exists. Grizzly Bears is unaffected and no Plains are tapped.
